#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Printer panel conversations against the live model, without the app.

The printer panel's assistant is a system prompt (printerInstructions.ts),
eight printer tools and the chat. This script sends the model the same
requests the app sends, answers the tools the way the app answers them for a
fixed printer, and checks what the model does. A case is a short scripted
conversation; each run of it is one sample of a model that answers
differently each time, so a case is run many times and the result is a count.

What the app sends, reproduced here:
  - instructions: rendered from printerInstructions.ts by render_prompt.mjs,
    so an edit to the prompt is tested without building anything;
  - tools: printer_tools.json, the app's own tool list for the printer panel
    (test_openai_responses_agent.cpp fails if it drifts from the registry);
  - input: earlier turns as the app replays them -- each assistant message's
    words, then the tool calls it made with their results, as function_call
    (no item id) and function_call_output -- then this turn's message, then
    this turn's calls and results (AgentHost::make_agent_request,
    OpenAIResponsesAgent::initial_input). A call the app refused before it ran
    (bad arguments) was never recorded, so it is not replayed.
The app streams its requests; this script does not. Nothing else differs.

Usage:
  OPENAI_API_KEY=... tests/printer_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py [--runs N]
      [--must-pass N] [--case NAME] [--jobs 5] [--model gpt-5.4-mini] [--verbose]
      [--endpoint URL --key-env NAME]

Another model is tried through any Responses API endpoint, such as
OpenRouter's, with its key in the variable --key-env names. The judge stays on
OpenAI (OPENAI_API_KEY), so two models' counts are judged alike.

Without --runs, the cases run share RUN_BUDGET conversations: 5 runs each for
20 cases, fewer when there are more, never more than MAX_RUNS for one case.

Exit code 0 when every case passes at least --must-pass of its runs
(default: all of them), 1 otherwise. Needs python3 and node, and the page's
npm install (src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/node_modules) for esbuild.
"""

import argparse
import concurrent.futures
import json
import os
import pathlib
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import time
import urllib.error
import urllib.request

HERE = pathlib.Path(__file__).resolve().parent
ENDPOINT = os.environ.get("JUSPRIN_OPENAI_ENDPOINT", "https://api.openai.com/v1/responses")
# The judge stays on OpenAI whichever endpoint the model under test is on, so
# counts from two models are judged alike.
JUDGE_ENDPOINT = "https://api.openai.com/v1/responses"
MODEL = "gpt-5.4-mini"  # OpenAIResponsesConfig's default model
JUDGE_MODEL = "gpt-5.5-2026-04-23"  # pinned, so a count moves only when the prompt does
# UTF-8 throughout: on Windows, Python otherwise reads text as the system code
# page and garbles "×" and curly quotes before the model sees them.
TOOLS = json.loads((HERE / "printer_tools.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
MAX_REQUESTS_PER_TURN = 8
# Conversations one invocation runs by default, shared by the cases it runs,
# and the most one case gets from that share.

def main():
    sys.stdout.reconfigure(encoding="utf-8")  # the logs show replies as the model wrote them
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__.split("\n\n")[0])
    parser.add_argument("--case", action="append", choices=sorted(CASES), help="run only this case (repeatable)")
    parser.add_argument("--runs", type=int, help=f"runs per case (default: {RUN_BUDGET} shared by the cases run, "
                                                 f"at most {MAX_RUNS} each)")
    parser.add_argument("--must-pass", type=int, help="runs per case that must pass (default: all)")
    parser.add_argument("--jobs", type=int, default=5, help="runs in parallel (default 5)")
    parser.add_argument("--model", default=MODEL)
    parser.add_argument("--endpoint", default=ENDPOINT,
                        help="Responses API endpoint of the model under test, e.g. https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/responses")
    parser.add_argument("--key-env", default="OPENAI_API_KEY", help="environment variable holding that endpoint's key")
    parser.add_argument("--provider", action="append",
                        help="OpenRouter only: serve every request from this host (repeatable, in order of preference)")
    parser.add_argument("--verbose", action="store_true", help="print every run's conversation, not only failures")
    args = parser.parse_args()
    key = os.environ.get(args.key_env)
    if not key or not os.environ.get("OPENAI_API_KEY"):
        sys.exit(f"{args.key_env} is required, and OPENAI_API_KEY for the judge")
    names = args.case or sorted(CASES)
    if args.runs is None:
        args.runs = max(1, min(MAX_RUNS, RUN_BUDGET // len(names)))
    must_pass = args.runs if args.must_pass is None else args.must_pass

    ok = True
    for name in names:
        case_class = CASES[name]
        prompt = render(case_class.session)
        with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor(max_workers=args.jobs) as pool:
            results = list(pool.map(lambda _: run_once(case_class, prompt, key, args.model, args.endpoint, args.provider),
                                    range(args.runs)))
        passed = sum(1 for result in results if result[0])
        for index, (good, detail, log) in enumerate(results, 1):
            print(f"{name} run {index}/{args.runs}: {detail}")
            if args.verbose or not good:
                for line in log:
                    print("    " + line.replace("\n", "\n    "))
        print(f"{name}: {passed} of {args.runs} passed (needs {must_pass})")
        ok = ok and passed >= must_pass
    sys.exit(0 if ok else 1)

14	runs several times, in parallel, and reports a count. By default one invocation
15	runs at most 100 conversations (`RUN_BUDGET`), shared by the cases it runs: 5
16	each for 20 cases, fewer each when there are more, and at most 20 for a case
17	run alone. `--runs N` sets the count per case instead; use it to look closer at
18	one case. By default every run must pass; `--must-pass N` lowers the bar.
19	`--verbose` prints every conversation, not only the failed ones.

21	## Judging a prompt change
22	
23	Run the cases before and after the edit and compare the counts. The script
24	renders the prompt from the TypeScript source on every run, so nothing needs
25	building. At the default five runs a case catches a behaviour that fails
26	often, not one that fails one time in twenty; when a case fails, or to judge
27	the edit it was written for, run that case alone, where it gets 20 runs.
28	Differences of a few runs out of 20 are noise; look for a clear gap.
29

31	prompt, so a line written for one of them reaches the other two; a fix is one
32	whose own case improves while no other case drops.
33

35	replies: a `Choices:` line the page draws as intended (on the last line, two
36	to four choices under 30 characters, or Done alone; read as

38	out (profile, preset, catalog, a tool's name). A reply that breaks one fails
39	its run, whatever the case checks.

42	Those ask a stronger model (`JUDGE_MODEL`, pinned) one narrow yes-or-no
43	question about the conversation's last reply, and the run prints its reason.

content.content:
# Printer panel prompt tests

The printer panel's assistant is a system prompt
(`src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/printerInstructions.ts`), eight printer
tools, and the chat. `run_prompt_tests.py` sends the live model the same
requests the app sends. It answers the tools the way the app answers them for
a fixed printer, then checks what the model did. The app does not run.

```bash
OPENROUTER_API_KEY=... OPENAI_API_KEY=... tests/printer_prompt/run_prompt_tests.py
```

Prompts are judged on DeepSeek V4 Flash through OpenRouter, served only by the
hosts that answer the app's notes (decided 2026-09-28; see "Which model").
`OPENROUTER_API_KEY` is for that model, `OPENAI_API_KEY` for the judge.

A run is one sample of a model that answers differently each time, so each case
runs several times, in parallel, and reports a count. By default one invocation
runs at most 100 conversations (`RUN_BUDGET`), shared by the cases it runs: 3
each for the 28 cases, and at most 20 for a case run alone. `--runs N` sets the count per case instead; use it to look closer at
one case. By default every run must pass; `--must-pass N` lowers the bar.
`--verbose` prints every conversation, not only the failed ones.

## Judging a prompt change

Run the cases before and after the edit and compare the counts; "Baseline"
below has the counts to start from. The script renders the prompt from the
TypeScript source on every run, so nothing needs building. At the default
three runs a case catches a behaviour that fails often, not one that fails one
time in twenty; when a case fails, or to judge
the edit it was written for, run that case alone, where it gets 20 runs.
Differences of a few runs out of 20 are noise; look for a clear gap.

Run every case, not only the one the edit is for. The three sessions share one
prompt, so a line written for one of them reaches the other two; a fix is one
whose own case improves while no other case drops.

Before a prompt change ships, run it once more with `--app`: the app's own
model, gpt-5.4-mini on OpenAI. The two models fail in different places, and
people talk to the app's.

Every reply in every case is also held to the rules the prompt sets for all
replies: a `Choices:` line the page draws as intended (on the last line, two
to four choices under 30 characters, or Done alone; read as
`replyChoices.ts` reads it), and none of the internal words the prompt rules
out (profile, preset, catalog, a tool's name). A reply that breaks one fails
its run, whatever the case checks.

A few checks are about what a reply says, which no string test can read.
Those ask a stronger model (`JUDGE_MODEL`, pinned) one narrow yes-or-no

'Rules for finding the printer:\n' +
  '- Start with just the printer model. Do not ask for nozzle, plate or filament first; the plate and filament are ' +
  'chosen when preparing a print.\n' +
  '- The person names one model plainly: call printer_identify with it, then add it with printer_add, with the nozzle ' +
  'it ships with unless they said another. Then say which nozzle it was set up with and that you can change it if ' +
  'theirs is different. One model fits a photo or a vague description: show it with printer_identify and ask if that ' +
  'is it. ' +
  'Two or three genuinely fit: call it with all of them and ask which, one choice each. More than three fit: do not ' +
  'call it; ask one question that narrows it down, or offer to browse the full list (printer_manual_setup). Nothing ' +
  "fits, or it isn't a filament printer: say so, offer the full list, and never offer a closest substitute.\n" +
  '- A name that is the start of more than one model is not one model, even when it equals one of them: "prusa mk4" ' +
  'begins Prusa MK4, MK4S and MK4S HF, so it is three printers.\n' +
  '- A photo names a model only from a readable name or printed size; going by shape alone, ask for a photo of the ' +
  'label. Never judge size from how big it looks. A clone uses the model it copies.\n' +
  '- Pass a nozzle only when the person or a photo said its size, and never substitute a size they did not confirm. ' +
  'After unknown_nozzle, name the sizes supported for that model and ask them to check the marking on the nozzle.\n' +
  '- alreadyYours means settings for the same model were saved before, not that this machine was added.\n' +
  '- When the app says the person undid adding a printer, that printer is removed: say so in a few words and ask ' +
  'which printer they have, unless they already said. Do not add the same model again unless they ask for it.\n' +
  'Rules for changing a printer:\n' +
  '- Work out what physically changed and change only that with printer_change; afterwards say what that means ("Every ' +
  'project that uses the K1 now slices for 0.6 mm.") and end with "Choices: Done". If what changed is unclear, ask. ' +
  'Putting it back is the same tool.\n' +
  "- The plate belongs to each project, not the printer. Nozzle material, such as hardened steel, isn't tracked.\n" +
  '- A nozzle mismatch reported by the printer is something to offer to fix with printer_change.\n' +
  '- printer_change saves the nozzle only. What is loaded comes from the printer itself when it is connected, and the ' +
  'filament a print uses is picked in the project, so when someone says what they loaded there is nothing to save.\n' +
  'Rules for connecting a printer:\n' +
  '- The connection tools act on the printer this is about, named below; a printer found on the network is only ever ' +
  'a deviceId.\n' +
  '- Connecting is optional; after adding, offer it once: end the reply to a successful printer_add with exactly ' +
  '"Want to connect it so you can send prints straight to it?" and then "Choices: Connect it | Not now". ' +
  'For a Bambu Lab printer, call printer_connection_status and ' +
  'connect to a printer it lists; with more than one, ask which. None listed means LAN mode is off or it is on another ' +
  'network: say where to turn LAN mode on (on the printer\'s screen, in its network settings; ask what they see rather ' +
  'than invent a menu). For Moonraker or OctoPrint, ask for the address they open it with in a browser, including its ' +
  'port when there is one, then call printer_connect.\n' +
  '- Never ask for a password, access code or API key in chat, and never repeat one: printer_connect shows a card where ' +
  'the person types it. If printer_connect comes back cancelled, say at most a few words; if the person wrote a message ' +
  'instead, answer that.\n' +
  '- "connecting" means the app is still waiting for the printer; its message says for how long. Say in one short ' +
  "line that you are checking and how long it can take, and answer anything the person says meanwhile; the app's " +
  'note says how it went. A failure that is a timeout means no response, not a wrong code.\n' +
  '- After a failed connection, say what went wrong in one sentence, then name the three ways forward: ' +
  'try again with the same address; enter the connection details in the printer settings ' +
  '(printer_manual_connection); or leave it for now, as the printer can prepare prints without a connection. If they ' +
  'leave it, say again that it can prepare prints, and that Connect… in its menu on Home is there for later, and end ' +
  'with "Choices: Done".\n' +
  'Rules for finishing:\n' +
  '- Once nothing is left to decide, say what that leaves them with, then end the reply with the line "Choices: Done", ' +
  'the one choice offered alone. That is after the person turns down connecting, after the app says the connection ' +
  'is verified, after they leave connecting for now, and after a successful printer_change. Never after printer_connect ' +
  'comes back cancelled: nothing failed and nothing was declined, so that reply is those few words with no choices. ' +
  'For example:\n' +
  'It is connected, so you can send prints straight to it.\nChoices: Done\n' +
  '- Call printer_setup_finish only when the person says they are done, such as tapping Done; it closes this ' +
  'conversation, so never call it on your own.\n';

1	// What the model is told in the printer panel: its system prompt. Written
2	// here, on the page, and handed to the app with printer_instructions; the app
3	// sends it with every request of the session and offers every printer tool
4	// in every session. The facts it states -- the printer list, what is on the
5	// network, the printer this is about -- come from the app in the session's
6	// `context`.
7	//
8	// The rules come in sections, and a session is sent the ones it can reach:
9	// finding and adding a printer only while adding one, so a conversation about
10	// a printer the person already has is not steered toward adding it; changing,
11	// connecting and finishing in every session, since each can lead to them.
12	
13	import type { PrinterSessionPayload } from './bridge/protocol';
14	import { numberText, sizesText } from './printerWords';
15	
16	const CORE =
17	  "You are JusPrin's printer assistant, talking to someone who may never have used a slicer. Each conversation is " +
18	  'about one thing, stated at the end: adding a printer so they can prepare prints for it, changing a printer they ' +
19	  'already have, or connecting a printer over the network if that helps them and they want it.\n' +
20	  'Use plain language, one to three short sentences. Ask one question at a time, and say where to find any answer you ask ' +
21	  'for. Avoid internal terms such as profile, preset and catalog.\n' +
22	  'When the person plainly states what to do or what changed ("I put a 0.6 nozzle on it", "yes, add it", "put it back ' +
23	  'to 0.4"), do it: call the tool without asking again. When you are guessing -- which model from a photo or a vague ' +
24	  'description, which printer on the network -- ask first and stop: that reply calls no ' +
25	  'tool, and you act on the person\'s answer. ' +
26	  'After a tool result, say what happened in the person\'s terms. Never say something is done before a tool says so. ' +
27	  'Write every fact from the tools and the facts below, never from memory. Messages from the app (developer role) state ' +
28	  'what happened; they are facts, not requests.\n' +
29	  'What you can do here: find and add a printer, save the nozzle size on it, and connect it. Everything else about a ' +
30	  'printer that is set up -- its other settings, such as start g-code, bed size or speeds -- is in its printer ' +
31	  'settings on this computer, which printer_manual_connection opens: say so, and offer to open them. Never give a ' +
32	  'reason you cannot help that the tools and the facts below do not state, such as the printer needing to be added ' +
33	  'or connected.\n' +
34	  'Answers to tap: whenever your message asks a yes-or-no question, asks the person to confirm something, or asks ' +
35	  'them to pick from a few options, its last line must be "Choices: first | second | third" -- two to four short ' +
36	  'answers (Done, below, is the only one offered alone), each under 30 characters, written as the person would say ' +
37	  'them. The person taps one instead of typing, and it reaches you as their own message. Leave the line out only ' +
38	  'when you need free text, such as an address or a model name, and never write anything after it.';
39	
40	// Where they stand matters: moved from here to the end of the finding rules,
41	// the example of asking "Is that it?" followed the rule to add a model named
42	// plainly, and the model asked instead of adding (0 of 3, was 2 of 3).
43	const FINDING_EXAMPLES =
44	  ' Examples:\n' +
45	  'From your photo, that looks like the Anycubic Kobra 3. Is that it?\nChoices: Yes, that is it | Different printer\n' +
46	  'Which one is yours?\nChoices: Prusa MK4 | Prusa MK4S | Prusa MK4S HF\n';
47	
48	// A size the model does not ship is refused by printer_change as well as by

51	const NOZZLE_SIZES =

53	  'After unknown_nozzle, name the sizes supported for that model and ask them to check the marking on the nozzle.\n';

content.text:
The prompt change is done and passes: nothing is worse, and the reported bug case is 20/20 on both models.

**What changed in `printerInstructions.ts`:**
- **Change and Connect conversations** now get:
  - their own opening goal ("Their printer is already set up so they can prepare prints for it…");
  - a line near the end saying the printer is already set up and prepares prints whether or not it's connected;
  - a scope rule: other settings such as start g-code live in the printer's settings on this computer, which `printer_manual_connection` opens, and the model must never give a reason it can't help that the tools and facts don't state, such as "it needs to be added or connected".

  They no longer get the finding and adding rules, the "Is that it?" examples, or the post-add connect offer.
- **The Add prompt is byte-for-byte what it was.** The tests now check that.
- The nozzle-size rule is now sent in every conversation, because `printer_change` can refuse a size too.

**Getting there, the approach earlier in this conversation caught three regressions:**
1. Moving the "Is that it?" examples next to the add rule made the model ask instead of add.
2. Splitting the rules dropped the nozzle-size rule from Change conversations: the app's model fell to 11/20 on naming the sizes.
3. The main one: a shared goal line naming all three conversations, and the scope rule in the shared core, **each** made DeepSeek stop adding plainly named printers. At 20 runs, `add-not-now-done` fell from 19 to 3. So Add keeps its measured wording, and the new text reaches only Change and Connect.

**Final result, old and new run side by side:**

| | Old | New |
|---|---|---|
| Full suite, DeepSeek | 74/84 | 77/84 |
| Full suite, app's model | 78/84 | 79/84 |
| Kobra 3 start g-code case, 20 runs, DeepSeek | 18/20 | **20/20** |
| Same case, app's model | 19/20 | **20/20** |
| Unshipped nozzle, app's model, 20 runs | 20/20 (earlier run) | 20/20 |

No Change or Connect case scored lower. The small Add differences are noise, since that prompt didn't change. All 213 page tests pass and the type check is clean.

**Changes to the harness:**
- `--prompt-rev REV` renders the prompt from a git revision, so you can run "before" against "after" at the same time without touching the checkout.
- The README records the paired baseline, the measured run-to-run noise (the same prompt scored 76, 76 and 74 of 84), and says to compare against a before run made alongside the after run, not a recorded baseline.

**Still open:**
- "bambu a1" still fails nearly every run on both models. This change didn't set out to fix it.
- I haven't checked this in the running app, only through the harness.

Nothing is committed. Want me to commit the prompt change and the harness separately?

content.text:
Yes to the regression question, with limits. Details on the "bambu a1" case follow.

## Did step 2 cause any regressions?

As far as the suite can see, no:
- **Add conversations can't have regressed from this change.** The Add prompt is byte-for-byte what it was, and a unit test now checks that.
- **No Change or Connect case scored lower** than the old prompt, run side by side on both models.
- **Totals went up:** DeepSeek 74 → 77 of 84, the app's model 78 → 79.
- **The two cases most at risk held at 20 runs:** the start g-code case (20/20 on both) and the unshipped nozzle case (20/20).

Three limits on that answer:
1. **3 runs per case only catches frequent failures.** A Change or Connect behaviour that now fails 1 time in 10 could slip through. Only the start g-code case and the nozzle case got 20 runs.
2. **The suite only covers what we wrote.** One path isn't covered at all: someone in a Change conversation asking to add a *different* printer ("I also have a Prusa, add it"). The model still has the add tools there but no longer has the finding rules.
3. **Only tested through the harness, not in the running app.** The app's C++ side didn't change, and the page's own tests pass.

## The `add-name-starts-two` case

**What it does:** in an Add conversation the person says "bambu a1". The printer list has both "Bambu Lab A1" and "Bambu Lab A1 mini". The case passes when nothing is added and the judge confirms the reply asks which of the two it is.

**Why it exists:** it guards a rule added in `7f66e75b07`: *"A name that is the start of more than one model is not one model, even when it equals one of them."* That commit's own measurement already had "bambu a1" at 0 of 3 with the rule in place, so the rule never worked for this input.

**What the models do:** they treat "bambu a1" as a plainly named model. They look up the A1 alone and add it straight away, following the rule for plain names instead of the rule for ambiguous ones. The app's model:

> person: bambu a1
> tool: printer_identify ["BBL/Bambu Lab A1"]
> tool: printer_add BBL/Bambu Lab A1, nozzle 0.4

**Across every run today** (14 batches of 3 runs):

| Model | Result |
|---|---|
| gpt-5.4-mini (the app's) | 0/3 in every batch |
| DeepSeek V4 Flash | 0 or 1 of 3 per batch |
| MiniMax-M3 | 2/3 |
| MiMo-V2.6-Pro | 3/3, the only model that asked |

**Two harness caveats:**
- The A1's lookup answer was written from its printer profile, not recorded from the app. Any A1 add also gets a "this test has no answer" error, because no A1 add was recorded. That doesn't change the result, since the failure has already happened when the model adds without asking. But it hid something: in one DeepSeek run the model got **two failed adds** and then said *"Your Bambu Lab A1 is all set!"* That breaks "never say something is done before a tool says so", and **no case checks for it**. It's worth its own case: a failed `printer_add`, then a check that the reply doesn't claim success.
- 3 runs is enough here because the failure is so consistent.

**Whether the expected behaviour is right is a product decision for you:**
- **Keep the rule (ask "A1 or A1 mini?"):** a small delay for people who really have an A1. It avoids silently setting up the wrong printer for someone who wrote "a1" as shorthand for the mini, which has a different build volume (180 vs 256 mm) and so slices wrong. Undo exists, but only if they notice.
- **Drop the rule for exact names:** "bambu a1" means the A1, and the case changes to expect an add. This matches what the models already do, but "prusa mk4" would then mean the MK4 alone, which the current `add-choose-from-three` case says is wrong.

If you keep the rule, the prompt needs a stronger form of it, probably an example showing this exact situation, because the current wording has never worked. I'd measure that the same way: side by side with `--prompt-rev HEAD`, the whole suite at 3 runs per case, plus this case at 20 runs.

This is the slowest part. An app build in a fresh tree has taken about 40 minutes on this machine before.

**2. Commit, in two commits:**
- **the harness:** the 28 cases, the judge, the checks on every reply, the 100-run budget, the UTF-8 fix, host pinning, `--app`, `--prompt-rev`, the default model, and the README with the baseline;
- **the prompt change:** `printerInstructions.ts` and its tests, with the paired before/after numbers in the message.

Two commits, so the prompt change can be reviewed and reverted on its own.

- There's no case for the model claiming success after a failed tool call. DeepSeek said "Your Bambu Lab A1 is all set!" after two failed adds.
- There's no case for someone in a Change conversation asking to add a different printer.

`agent-docs/jusprin/mcp-tool-extension-guide.md` (around line 95, and its tool table ~line 354) says the panel offers EXACTLY ONE tool per mode: printer_identify when adding, printer_change when changing; it also says "A Change session that could also identify a printer could clear the card of the printer it is about." But today `PrinterConversation::session_tools()` returns all eight tools in every mode, and the header of `src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/AgentUI/src/printerInstructions.ts` says "offers every printer tool in every session".

Find out, with evidence (commit shas, dates, quotes kept short):
1. The rationale for "one tool per mode": which commit introduced it (likely 7f66e75b07 "Let the model understand the printer, and the app do what it already knows", 2026-09-18), what reasons its message, the guide, `agent-docs/jusprin/architecture.md`, `product-definition.md` or other agent-docs give. Is the "clear the card" reason still applicable (does the pinned card still exist)?
2. When and why the code moved to all tools in every mode: find the commit that changed `session_tools()` (use `git log -L` or `git log -S'session_tools' -p -- src/slic3r/GUI/JusPrin/PrinterSetup/PrinterConversation.cpp`), and quote its stated reasons. Was the guide updated then? Is there any stated reason why Add needs change/connect tools or Change needs add tools (e.g. add-then-connect in one conversation, add then change nozzle)?
3. Check past agent sessions with the `entire` CLI: run `entire search --json "one tool per mode"` and similar queries ("session_tools", "every printer tool", "printer_identify printer_change mode", "tools per mode") — see `entire search --help` first. Report anything relevant (session ids, what was decided and why). If the CLI hangs, use a timeout (e.g. `timeout 60 entire search ...`) and move on.
4. Also note other places the code enforces per-mode behaviour instead of the tool list: e.g. `preflight_tool`, `execute_tool` refusals like "no_printer", app checks that refuse printer_change in Add mode or printer_add in Change mode, and whether printer_add in a Change session would actually add a second printer or be refused. Read PrinterConversation.cpp to answer precisely.
5. Anything in the guide's general principles about exposing tools (e.g. "every tool loads", minimal tool sets, tool count) that bears on this.

Report compactly: a timeline, the stated rationales (for one-per-mode and for all-in-every-mode), what the code actually enforces per mode, and whether the guide's statement is simply stale or reflects a still-valid design intent. Say "unclear" rather than guess.

input.description: Research tool exposure best practices
input.prompt:
Web research (use WebSearch and WebFetch; modify no files). Today is 2026-09-28.

Question: for an LLM agent with several conversation "modes" (here: a 3D-printer setup chat with Add, Change and Connect conversations; 8 function tools in total: identify/add a printer, open a full printer list, change nozzle, check connection status, connect, open printer settings, finish/close), is it better to offer every tool in every mode, or only the tools each mode needs (dynamic/scoped tool exposure)? A conversation can legitimately flow Add -> Connect -> Done, and Change -> Connect. Observed problem: in a Change conversation, the model sometimes called printer_add/printer_identify (tools meant for Add) when confused.

Find current best-practice guidance, with URLs, from primary sources where possible:
- Anthropic (e.g. "Building effective agents", "Writing effective tools for agents", "Effective context engineering for AI agents", tool-use docs; anything on tool count, tool search / deferred tools, restricting tools per state).
- OpenAI (function calling guide, GPT-5.x prompting guides, Agents SDK guidance on tools per agent, handoffs, `tool_choice`/allowed_tools — note OpenAI's Responses API has an `allowed_tools` option in tool_choice that restricts callable tools while keeping the full list for caching; confirm and cite).
- Google / others if relevant; research on tool-selection accuracy vs number of tools (e.g. tool-overload papers, RAG-MCP, "less is more" tool selection).
- Guidance on state machines / "workflows vs agents": restricting actions to what the current state allows, and enforcing invariants in code (validation/refusal) versus hoping the prompt steers.
- Prompt caching implications of changing the tool list between turns (OpenAI and Anthropic both cache on the prefix incl. tools), and the allowed_tools trick.

Then give your own synthesis: when to scope tools per mode vs keep them all; how to handle legitimate cross-mode flows (Add->Connect) without breaking; the role of server-side refusal as a backstop. Keep it compact (bullets with citations). Say when a claim is vendor opinion vs measured.

<result>I recommend scoping the tools to each conversation state and keeping a refusal in code behind it. With 8 tools, the number of tools is not what goes wrong. Your Change conversations call Add tools because those tools are offered in a state where they are invalid. That is a state-machine problem, and the prompt cannot enforce it. The one thing that decides how you implement the scoping is which API you call, because of prompt caching.

## What the sources say

**Tool count alone is not your problem**
- Anthropic's tool search docs say plain tool calling is "a better fit when you have fewer than 10 tools". They put the drop in selection accuracy at "30–50 available tools". Vendor claim, measured on their own evals, raw numbers not published. https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/tool-search-tool
- OpenAI's function calling guide says "Aim for fewer than 20 functions available at the start of a turn", and calls it "just a soft suggestion". Vendor opinion. https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/function-calling
- OpenAI's practical guide to agents says the issue "isn't solely the number of tools, but their similarity or overlap". Some teams manage more than 15 distinct tools, while others struggle with fewer than 10 overlapping ones. Vendor observation from customer work, not a benchmark. https://cdn.openai.com/business-guides-and-resources/a-practical-guide-to-building-agents.pdf (text copy: https://gist.github.com/testy-cool/86cafd426ba22e3e8c1d6d2c853506c4)

**Overlapping or ambiguous tools are the known failure**
- Anthropic's "Writing tools for agents": when tools overlap or have a vague purpose, "agents can get confused about which ones to use". Vendor opinion. https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/writing-tools-for-agents
- Anthropic's context engineering post calls bloated tool sets "one of the most common failure modes". It adds that if a human engineer cannot say which tool fits a situation, an agent can't either. It recommends a "minimal viable set of tools". Vendor opinion. https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/effective-context-engineering-for-ai-agents
- OpenAI recommends enums and object structure "to prevent invalid states", plus "use code where possible" and "Don't make the model fill arguments you already know". Vendor opinion. https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/function-calling

**Research on showing fewer tools (measured, but at much larger tool counts than yours)**
- RAG-MCP, arXiv 2505.03275: retrieving only the relevant tools raised selection accuracy from 13.62% to 43.13% and cut prompt tokens by more than half. Preprint, run on hundreds of MCP tools. https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.03275
- "Less is More", arXiv 2411.15399: cutting 46 tools to 19 improved function selection on small edge models. https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.15399
- "How Many Tools Should an LLM Agent See?", arXiv 2605.24660: shorter adaptive shortlists gave Claude Sonnet 4.6 93.1% selection accuracy versus 87.1% with a fixed 5 tools. Preprint, May 2026. https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.24660
- Anthropic reports its tool search took Opus 4 from 49% to 74% on large MCP libraries. Vendor measured. https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/advanced-tool-use
- None of this measures an 8-tool set. It shows the direction (fewer, relevant tools help), not how big the effect would be for you.

**Workflows vs agents, and state-dependent tools**
- "Building effective agents": workflows suit "well-defined tasks" where you can hardcode the path. The routing pattern "classifies an input and directs it to a specialized followup task". It also recommends "poka-yoke" tool design: change the arguments so mistakes are harder to make. https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/building-effective-agents
- OpenAI Agents SDK: `is_enabled` on a tool can be a function of the run's context and state. Disabled tools are "completely hidden from the LLM". The docs also say this "does not replace authorization" that depends on the arguments or the resource. https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/tools/
  - A related SDK issue describes one tool being offered before a workflow step and a different one after it, e.g. `draft_invoice` then `send_invoice`. This is the pattern for your Add→Connect flow. https://github.com/openai/openai-agents-python/issues/4626
- OpenAI's guide says to split into separate agents when prompts collect many if/then branches, or when clearer tool descriptions don't fix the errors. Guardrails should be "a layered defense", with each tool rated by risk. Vendor opinion.

**Prompt caching (documented behaviour)**
- **OpenAI (confirmed).** `tool_choice: {"type":"allowed_tools","mode":"auto"|"required","tools":[...]}` restricts which tools can be called while you keep passing the full list, "so you can maximize savings from prompt caching". The caching guide also says to keep tool definitions, order and schemas unchanged, and to use `tool_choice: "none"` rather than removing tools. https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/function-calling and https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/prompt-caching
- **Anthropic.**
  - The cache prefix order is tools, then system, then messages. Changing the tool definitions invalidates the entire cache, including the conversation history. Changing `tool_choice` invalidates only the messages part.
  - `tool_choice` accepts only auto, any, tool or none. There is no allowed-subset option.
  - Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5, Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 reject `any` and `tool` with a 400 error.
  - `defer_loading` with tool search keeps the cache intact, but it lets the model find tools; it does not stop it calling them. Anthropic also says it is not worth it under 10 tools.
  - Sources: https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/tool-use-with-prompt-caching and https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/tool-use/define-tools
- **Gemini** has `function_calling_config.allowed_function_names`, which works like OpenAI's `allowed_tools`. https://ai.google.dev/gemini-api/docs/function-calling. A figure of "~50 tools" came up only on third-party pages; I could not confirm it in Google's docs.

## Synthesis (my recommendation)

- **Scope the tools, but compute the allowed set from state, not from the conversation's label.**
  - Change conversation: allow change nozzle, open printer settings, check connection status, connect, finish.
  - Add conversation: allow identify/add and the full printer list. Once a printer has been added, also allow check connection status, connect and finish. That covers Add→Connect→Done.
  - Change→Connect already works, because the connect tools are in the Change set.
  - Each state's allowed set should include the tools for the transitions it may take next. This is the `draft_invoice`→`send_invoice` pattern above.
- **Keep the tool list identical on every turn and restrict through `tool_choice` where the API allows it.**
  - On OpenAI, use `allowed_tools`. On Gemini, use `allowed_function_names`.
  - On Anthropic, the only way to hide tools is to change the `tools` array, which invalidates the whole cache.
  - A new conversation starts with an empty cache anyway, so you lose nothing by choosing the tool set once when the conversation starts.
  - Changing it mid-conversation (for example when Add finishes adding a printer) costs one uncached re-read of the history. For short setup chats that is cheap. If it isn't acceptable, keep all 8 tools and rely on the refusal below plus clear descriptions.
- **Always refuse in code, whatever the model is shown.**
  - The layer that owns the conversation state should reject an out-of-state call and return an explicit error as the tool result. For example: "printer_add is not available while changing an existing printer's settings; to add a different printer, finish this conversation first."
  - Don't silently ignore the call. A visible error lets the model correct itself, and it matches the repo's AGENTS.md rule that invariants are enforced by the layer that owns the decision.
  - OpenAI's own SDK docs say hiding a tool does not replace authorization, so scoping and refusal are complementary, not alternatives.
- **Reduce the overlap as well.**
  - Say in each description when not to use the tool, e.g. "Only for adding a printer that is not yet set up; never while changing an existing printer."
  - Fill in the printer you are acting on from state rather than asking the model for it.
  - Consider letting the finish tool carry the outcome so there are fewer exits to choose between.
- **Add the observed failures as regression tests.**
  - Replay the confused Change transcripts and assert that the Add tools are either not offered or refused with the guiding error.
  - Add a test that Add→Connect→Done and Change→Connect still complete.</result>

- OpenAI's function calling guide says "Aim for fewer than 20 functions available at the start of a turn", and calls it "just a soft suggestion". Vendor opinion. https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/guides/function-calling
- OpenAI's practical guide to agents says the issue "isn't solely the number of tools, but their similarity or overlap". Some teams manage more than 15 distinct tools, while others struggle with fewer than 10 overlapping ones. Vendor observation from customer work, not a benchmark. https://cdn.openai.com/business-guides-and-resources/a-practical-guide-to-building-agents.pdf (text copy: https://gist.github.com/testy-cool/86cafd426ba22e3e8c1d6d2c853506c4)

- Anthropic's context engineering post calls bloated tool sets "one of the most common failure modes". It adds that if a human engineer cannot say which tool fits a situation, an agent can't either. **Research on showing fewer tools (measured, but at much larger tool counts than yours)**
- RAG-MCP, arXiv 2505.03275: retrieving only the relevant tools raised selection accuracy from 13.62% to 43.13% and cut prompt tokens by more than half. Preprint, run on hundreds of MCP tools. https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.03275
- "Less is More", arXiv 2411.15399: cutting 46 tools to 19 improved function selection on small edge models. https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.15399

It also recommends "poka-yoke" tool design: change the arguments so mistakes are harder to make. https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/building-effective-agents
- OpenAI Agents SDK: `is_enabled` on a tool can be a function of the run's context and state. Disabled tools are "completely hidden from the LLM". The docs also say this "does not replace authorization" that depends on the arguments or the resource. https://openai.github.io/openai-agents-python/tools/

  - Changing it mid-conversation (for example when Add finishes adding a printer) costs one uncached re-read of the history. For short setup chats that is cheap. If it isn't acceptable, keep all 8 tools and rely on the refusal below plus clear descriptions.

  - OpenAI's own SDK docs say hiding a tool does not replace authorization, so scoping and refusal are complementary, not alternatives.
- **Reduce the overlap as well.**
  - Say in each description when not to use the tool, e.g. "Only for adding a printer that is not yet set up; never while changing an existing printer."
  - Fill in the printer you are acting on from state rather than asking the model for it.
  - Consider letting the finish tool carry the outcome so there are fewer exits to choose between.
- **Add the observed failures as regression tests.**
  - Replay the confused Change transcripts and assert that the Add tools are either not offered or refused with the guiding error.
  - Add a test that Add→Connect→Done and Change→Connect still complete.</result>

<result>The guide's "one tool per mode" statement is stale. It was a deliberate design for a panel that no longer exists: the design was reversed on purpose on 2026-09-23, the guide was never updated, and nothing today says the old constraint should come back. There is one live pressure in its direction, described under "What's left of the old intent".

## Timeline

| Date | Commit | What `session_tools()` offered |
|---|---|---|
| 09-17 | `0e55c4f9be` | All four tools of that time (`printer_catalog_search`, `printer_propose`, `printer_suggest`, `printer_change`) in every mode. |
| 09-18 | `7f66e75b07` | One tool per mode: Add got `printer_identify`, Change got `printer_change`. This commit added the guide lines at ~95, ~289 and the two table rows. |
| 09-22 | `67577ad993` | Connect mode got no tools at all. |
| 09-22 | `4d4f9e466b` | "Replace printer summary card…": the pinned card was removed from the page. |
| 09-23 | `8334b3395b` | All eight tools in every mode. The code comment and the per-mode test were replaced by "every session offers every printer tool…". The guide was not touched. |
| 09-27 | `492fdb5531` | Edited the guide's `printer_change` table row but left "Change mode only". |

`bd81401da2` and `dae85d7970` (both 09-18) and `a9ec0277f5` (09-27) also edited the guide and left the one-per-mode text as it was.

## Why one tool per mode (`7f66e75b07`)

- **Commit message:** "the model decides and one tool per mode checks and carries out". The problem it was fixing was the app ordering the model around, plus a keyword search that misidentified printers. It gives no separate argument for restricting the tools.
- **Code comment and guide:** "A Change session that could identify a printer could also clear the card of the printer it is about."
- **What "the card" meant:** the pinned facts header (Printer, Nozzle, Plate, Filament). At `7f66e75b07`, `identify()` called `clear_proposal()`, which wiped those facts, so an identify call in Change mode would have blanked the header for the saved printer.
- **Is that reason still valid?** No. The pinned card was dropped from the page on 09-22 and its last C++ traces were deleted in `8334b3395b`. Today `identify()` only appends a picture-card block and clears nothing.
- **Other supporting text:** the guide's cache and size measurements for one definition per session. That is evidence about cost, not a reason for the rule.
- **Other docs:** `product-definition.md` has nothing on this. `architecture.md:137` says "The app decides which one tool each mode offers", which is equally stale.

## Why all tools in every mode (`8334b3395b` and its sessions)

- **Commit message:** "one assistant tool per phase" is listed among the problems of the old three-phase flow. The new panel is "only a conversation: the assistant adds, changes and connects printers through eight tools".
- **Where it came from:** the untracked handoff doc `printer-setup-chat-handoff.md`, recorded in Entire checkpoint `01M385D8DNVF1S28Q960NWJVH5`. Its design came from session `5f00eae1-…` (checkpoint session index 2); session `54c192d0-…` (index 1) implemented it.
  - Its diagnosis: the panel had "a different single tool for the assistant in each phase. The assistant is not told when phases change." Also, `profile()` "removes all tools once a printer is added".
  - Its prescription: "Every one of them is available for the whole session: `profile().tool_names` lists all of them, always." It also says to delete "`ConversationMode` gating of tools (keep the mode only to choose the opening line and which printer the session is about)".
  - The earlier UX-review reply in that session describes the same root cause: "exactly one tool the model may call, and after the add the model gets no tools at all."
  - Kenneth's own prompts that day ask for the assistant to guide the whole process instead of phase-by-phase UI. He never discussed tool gating directly.
- **Stated need for crossing modes:**
  - Add needs the connect tools: the worked Add example goes identify → add → "Connect it" → connect → finish in one conversation.
  - Connect is described as "the same as the Add conversation from 'Connect it' onward".
  - "Put it back to 0.4" is handled by the same change tool.
  - Nothing anywhere says Change or Connect needs `printer_identify` or `printer_add`. No-one argued it; it followed from "all tools, always".
- **Entire search:** `entire search` fails with "no matching repositories found for [TheSpaghettiDetective/JusPrin]", and `--all-repos` returns 0 hits. The findings above come from grepping the transcripts stored locally under `refs/entire/checkpoints/*`. Later checkpoints that mention the phrase (`01M3GKE71E…`, `01M3HGGA28…`, `01M3JCF2Z2…`) only quote the guide or code. None revisits the decision.

## What the code enforces per mode today (`PrinterConversation.cpp`)

**Mode checks.** Nothing in `preflight_tool`, `execute_tool` or the registry checks `m_mode`. Mode only sets the opening, which printer the session is about, whether the catalog and network are in `context`, and whether a Bambu session opens on the plug-in notice. Guards are keyed to whether a saved printer exists:

- **Connect tools:** `preflight_tool` covers only `printer_connect`. It returns `no_printer` when `m_printer_name` isn't saved, then does device/address checks. `connection_status` and `printer_manual_connection` return the same `no_printer` refusal. In practice these fail in an Add session until something has been added.
- **`printer_add` in a Change or Connect session:** not refused. It saves a new printer and sets `m_printer_name` to it, so the session is now about the new printer. The mode stays Change or Connect.
  - The only refusal is `already_added`, for the same catalog id twice in one conversation.
  - `printer_manual_setup` behaves the same way when the wizard adds printers.
- **`printer_change`:** takes a `printerName` and changes any saved printer, not only the one the session is about. That also works in Add mode before anything is added. The guide's table row ("the one saved printer the panel is about… Change mode only", "checked before its card… Undo reverses it") is wrong on all counts: there is no card and no Undo now.
- **`printer_identify` in Change or Connect:** harmless. It adds a picture block.
- **`printer_setup_finish`:** closes the panel in every mode.
- **Tests that pin today's behaviour:**
  - `tests/agent/test_printer_conversation.cpp:297` "every session offers every printer tool…"
  - `test_printer_conversation.cpp:1781` "the model is offered every printer tool…"
  - `tests/agent/test_openai_responses_agent.cpp:157`

## What's left of the old intent

The uncommitted work in this worktree steers per mode through the prompt, not the tool list. `printerInstructions.ts` sends the finding/adding rules "only while adding one, so a conversation about a printer the person already has is not steered toward adding it". A new `shell_harness` check asserts that a Change-session question ("what's the current start g-code?") calls neither `printer_add` nor `printer_identify`. It was added because the reply "once offered to add it first" (2026-09-28).

That is the only evidence I found of add tools causing trouble outside Add. The guide's own principles name "transcripts showing the model choosing the wrong tool" as the thing that would change its "every tool loads" reading. Whether this bug counts as that is unclear: the transcript shows an offer to add, not a wrong call.

## Relevant general principles in the guide (~86–95)

- "Every registered tool loads on every turn", which keeps the tools array byte-identical and cacheable.
- The 20-definition budget is "a measured trigger, not a gate".
- A tool-set switcher that rewrites the tools array breaks the cache and "is not to be built".

Eight fixed tools per session fits these principles. The line-95 bullet presents the panel as "the exception to 'every tool loads'", which is no longer true.

content.text:
No, not yet. The app is still rebuilding: it's compiling the GUI code and hasn't linked yet. So the live app check and the two commits haven't happened. Here is where things stand in plain terms.

**The bug you reported:** in the chat for changing a printer that was already added, the assistant sometimes said "add this printer first" or "it needs to be connected" when asked about a setting like start g-code. It did that because the instructions never told it the printer was already set up, and never said where such settings live.

**What I built first: a way to test the instructions.** There was already a small test script that sends the model the same messages the app sends. I grew it from 9 to 28 test conversations:
- adding, changing and connecting a printer;
- questions the assistant can't answer with its tools;
- regressions: problems earlier fixes solved, found by reading the history of the instructions.

Each test runs a few times because the model varies. By default a full run is capped at about 100 conversations. On your decision it tests with DeepSeek V4 Flash through OpenRouter; a separate option runs the app's own model as a final check. Along the way I fixed a few things in the test script:
- On Windows it was garbling "×" and apostrophes.
- Some OpenRouter servers answer the app's notes with nothing, so the script now sends requests only to servers that answer them properly.

**What I changed in the instructions:**
- The change and connect chats now say the printer is already set up and can prepare prints whether or not it's connected.
- They say other settings, such as start g-code, are in the printer's settings on this computer, and offer to open them.
- They no longer get the rules for finding and adding a printer.
- The instructions for adding a printer are exactly what they were. My first attempt changed them too, and the tests caught that it made the assistant stop adding printers people named plainly, so I kept those instructions as they were.

**Result:** comparing old and new instructions side by side, the reported bug went from 18–19 of 20 to 20 of 20 on both models, and nothing else got worse. Your Bambu A1 z-offset example also passes 10 of 10 with the new instructions. I added a check for its specific mistake ("which printer is it?") to the existing test instead of adding a duplicate.

**Still to do:**
1. Finish the build, then run the app's scripted live test, which now asks the start g-code question in a real change chat.
2. Make two commits: the test script, then the instruction change.
3. Write up the tool question. In short, the guide saying "one tool per mode" is out of date: the app deliberately switched to offering all eight tools on 09-23, and nobody updated the guide. But nothing gives the change chat a reason to have the "add printer" tools, and models have used them wrongly there. So I'll recommend offering each chat only the tools it can need, with the app refusing out-of-place calls as a backstop. For example, adding a printer would keep the connect tools, because people add and then connect in the same chat.

Nothing is committed yet.

# CLAUDE.md - Testing Guide for OrcaSlicer

This guide provides comprehensive instructions for Claude Code when writing, maintaining, and understanding tests in the OrcaSlicer codebase.

## ⚠️ CRITICAL RULES - MUST FOLLOW

### 1. **SECTIONS IN LOOPS - NEVER REUSE NAMES**
❌ **WRONG**: Will cause unpredictable behavior
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Bad loop sections") {
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; ++i) {
        SECTION("Same name") {  // WRONG! Same name used multiple times
            REQUIRE(i >= 0);
        }
    }
}
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Use DYNAMIC_SECTION or incorporate counter
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Good loop sections") {
    for (int i = 0; i < 3; ++i) {
        DYNAMIC_SECTION("Section " << i) {  // Unique name per iteration
            REQUIRE(i >= 0);
        }
    }
}
```

### 2. **THREAD SAFETY - ASSERTIONS ARE NOT THREAD-SAFE**
❌ **WRONG**: Will cause undefined behavior or crashes
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Multi-threaded test") {
    std::vector<std::thread> threads;
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) {
        threads.emplace_back([]() {
            REQUIRE(some_calculation() == expected);  // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
        });
    }
}
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Synchronize results, test on main thread
```cpp
TEST_CASE("Multi-threaded test") {
    std::vector<std::thread> threads;
    std::atomic<int> passed{0};
    
    for (int i = 0; i < 4; ++i) {
        threads.emplace_back([&passed]() {
            if (some_calculation() == expected) {
                passed++;
            }
        });
    }
    
    for (auto& t : threads) t.join();
    REQUIRE(passed == 4);  // Test results on main thread
}
```

### 3. **EXPRESSION DECOMPOSITION - AVOID BINARY OPERATORS**
❌ **WRONG**: Cannot decompose properly
```cpp
REQUIRE(a > 0 && b < 10);  // Shows "false" on failure, not individual values
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Split into separate assertions
```cpp
REQUIRE(a > 0);
REQUIRE(b < 10);  // Each shows individual values on failure
```

### 4. **FLOATING POINT - NEVER USE APPROX**
❌ **WRONG**: Approx is deprecated and asymmetric
```cpp
REQUIRE(calculated_value == Catch::Approx(expected));  // Deprecated!
```

✅ **CORRECT**: Use floating point matchers
```cpp
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_value, WithinAbs(expected, 0.001));
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_value, WithinRel(expected, 0.01));  // 1% tolerance
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_value, WithinULP(expected, 4));     // 4 ULPs apart
```

### 5. **TEST ORDERING - ALWAYS USE RANDOM ORDER**
✅ **REQUIRED**: For CI/CD and development
```bash
# Essential flags for running tests
./tests --order rand --warn NoAssertions

# For test sharding (parallel execution), share random seed
./tests --order rand --shard-index 0 --shard-count 3 --rng-seed 0xBEEF
./tests --order rand --shard-index 1 --shard-count 3 --rng-seed 0xBEEF
./tests --order rand --shard-index 2 --shard-count 3 --rng-seed 0xBEEF
```

## Overview of OrcaSlicer's Testing Framework

OrcaSlicer uses **Catch2 v3** (currently v3.11.0, vendored in `tests/catch2/`) as its primary testing framework. The test suite is organized into several modules that mirror the project's architectural components:

> **Note**: Test files include the framework via `#include <catch2/catch_all.hpp>` (the v3 single-header convenience include). All v3 features described in this guide are available.

### Test Structure
```
tests/
├── CMakeLists.txt              # Main test configuration
├── catch_main.hpp              # Custom test reporter
├── libslic3r/                  # Core library tests (21 test files)
├── fff_print/                  # FFF printing tests (12 test files)
├── sla_print/                  # SLA printing tests (4 test files)
├── libnest2d/                  # 2D nesting tests
├── slic3rutils/               # Utility tests
├── data/                      # Test data files and meshes
└── catch2/                    # Catch2 framework files
```

### Build Integration
- Tests are built using CMake with `catch_discover_tests()` integration
- Each test module creates a separate executable (e.g., `libslic3r_tests`, `fff_print_tests`)
- Test data directory is available via `TEST_DATA_DIR` preprocessor definition
- Custom verbose console reporter provides detailed test output

## Catch2 Features Guide

### Basic Assertions
```cpp
// Primary assertions - stop test on failure
REQUIRE(expression);
REQUIRE_FALSE(expression);

// Continuing assertions - continue test after failure  
CHECK(expression);
CHECK_FALSE(expression);

// Non-failing checks - record result but don't fail test
CHECK_NOFAIL(expression);  // Useful for assumptions that might be violated
```

### Exception Testing
```cpp
// Verify no exception is thrown
REQUIRE_NOTHROW(function_call());

// Verify any exception is thrown
REQUIRE_THROWS(risky_function());

// Verify specific exception type
REQUIRE_THROWS_AS(function_call(), SpecificException);

// Verify exception message
REQUIRE_THROWS_WITH(function_call(), "Expected error message");

// Verify exception with matchers (for partial matching)

                       Catch::Matchers::Message("contains this"));
```

### Complex Assertions with Matchers
```cpp
#include <catch2/matchers/catch_matchers.hpp>

// String matchers
using Catch::Matchers::StartsWith;
using Catch::Matchers::EndsWith;
using Catch::Matchers::ContainsSubstring;
using Catch::Matchers::Equals;
using Catch::Matchers::Matches;  // Regex matching

REQUIRE_THAT(result_string, StartsWith("Expected prefix"));
REQUIRE_THAT(result_string, ContainsSubstring("middle part"));
REQUIRE_THAT(result_string, Matches(".*pattern.*"));

// Floating point matchers - ALWAYS use these instead of Approx!
using Catch::Matchers::WithinAbs;
using Catch::Matchers::WithinRel;
using Catch::Matchers::WithinULP;

REQUIRE_THAT(float_value, WithinAbs(expected, 0.001));     // Absolute tolerance
REQUIRE_THAT(float_value, WithinRel(expected, 0.01));      // Relative tolerance (1%)
REQUIRE_THAT(float_value, WithinULP(expected, 4));         // ULP difference (requires IEEE-754)

// Combining matchers

```

## Common Pitfalls and Solutions

### Floating-Point Comparisons

> **CRITICAL**: Never use Approx - it's deprecated due to asymmetry and other issues

❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
REQUIRE(calculated_volume == expected_volume);           // Exact equality
REQUIRE(calculated_volume == Catch::Approx(expected));   // Deprecated! Asymmetric!
```

✅ **Correct**: Always use floating point matchers
```cpp
// Absolute tolerance - good when values are near zero
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinAbs(expected_volume, 0.001));

// Relative tolerance - good for values with different magnitudes
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinRel(expected_volume, 0.01));  // 1% tolerance

// ULP (Units in Last Place) - most precise, requires IEEE-754
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, WithinULP(expected_volume, 4));

// Combined approach - relative OR absolute
REQUIRE_THAT(calculated_volume, 
    WithinRel(expected_volume, 0.001) || WithinAbs(0.0, 0.000001));

// Precision control for output
Catch::StringMaker<double>::precision = 15;  // Show more decimal places
```

### Why Approx is Problematic:
- **Asymmetric**: `Approx(10).epsilon(0.1) != 11.1` but `Approx(11.1).epsilon(0.1) == 10`
- **Double-only**: All computation done in `double`, causes issues with `float` inputs  
- **Default behavior**: Only uses relative comparison, so `Approx(0) == X` only works for `X == 0`

### Path Handling
❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
std::string path = TEST_DATA_DIR + "/model.obj";  // May have path separator issues
```

✅ **Correct**:
```cpp
std::string path = std::string(TEST_DATA_DIR) + "/model.obj";
// or use boost::filesystem for complex path operations
```

### Exception Testing
❌ **Incorrect**:
```cpp
bool threw_exception = false;
try {
    risky_function();
} catch (...) {
    threw_exception = true;
}
REQUIRE(threw_exception);
```

✅ **Correct**:
```cpp
REQUIRE_THROWS(risky_function());
// or for specific exceptions
REQUIRE_THROWS_AS(risky_function(), SpecificException);
```

### Thread Safety

⚠️ **CRITICAL**: Catch2 assertions are **NOT thread-safe** by default!

> **Note**: Catch2 v3.9.0+ has opt-in thread-safe assertions via `CATCH_CONFIG_EXPERIMENTAL_THREAD_SAFE_ASSERTIONS`. OrcaSlicer is on v3.11.0 but does not enable this flag, so assertions remain non-thread-safe by default.

❌ **Incorrect**: Will cause undefined behavior or crashes
```cpp
std::thread t([&]() {
    REQUIRE(threaded_operation() == expected);  // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
    CHECK(other_operation());                   // NOT THREAD-SAFE!
});
```

✅ **Correct**: Collect results, assert on main thread
```cpp
std::atomic<bool> success{false};
std::atomic<int> error_count{0};

std::thread t([&]() {
    // Do work in thread, collect results
    bool result1 = (threaded_operation() == expected);
    bool result2 = other_operation();
    
    if (result1 && result2) {
        success = true;
    } else {
        error_count++;
    }
});

t.join();

// Assert results on main thread
REQUIRE(success);
REQUIRE(error_count == 0);
```

#### Thread Safety Rules:
- **REQUIRE family**: Would terminate process in spawned threads (throws exception with no try-catch)
- **CHECK family**: Not thread-safe, can corrupt internal state
- **SKIP, FAIL, SUCCEED**: Not thread-safe even with v3 thread-safe assertions
- **Message macros**: INFO, CAPTURE, WARN - not thread-safe
- **STATIC_REQUIRE/CHECK**: Not thread-safe (relies on runtime registration)

Use RAII and smart pointers in tests:

content.text:
All three parts are done: the check in the real app, the two commits, and the review of which tools each printer chat should have. The review says the guide is out of date. The code went too far the other way, though: each printer chat should get only the tools it can need, and the app should refuse any other tool call.

## 1. Checked in the real app
I rebuilt the test app from this branch and ran its scripted live printer test (`--printer-live`), which drives the real printer chat with the app's own model. All 115 checks passed. I added the start g-code question to its change chat, and the real app answered:

> "I can open the printer settings on this computer so you can see and edit things like start code. Do you want me to open them?"

It called no add or lookup tool.

## 2. Committed, on branch `claude/kobra3-gcode-prompt-bug-9d731f`
- `86b3bc555c`: the test harness, with 28 cases and the before-change baseline in its README.
- `ea4dec638f`: the prompt change, its unit tests, the new live check, and the updated baseline.

Nothing is pushed.

## 3. Tools in each printer chat

**Why the guide says "one tool per mode":** it was written on 09-18. Its one stated reason was that a lookup call in a change chat would wipe the card at the top showing the printer's details. That card was removed on 09-22, so the reason no longer applies.

**Why the code now offers all eight tools in every chat:** on 09-23 the panel was rebuilt as one conversation. The old one-tool-per-step design was one of the problems that change fixed: after adding a printer, the assistant had no tool left to connect it. Nobody updated the guide or `architecture.md`, and the guide's tool table also describes a confirmation card and an Undo that no longer exist.

So the guide is out of date, but the code isn't right either. No commit, doc or past session gives a reason for a change or connect chat to have the tools for adding a printer. They came along with "all tools, always", and they do damage:
- The app doesn't refuse them. `printer_add` in a change chat really saves a new printer and switches the chat to it.
- `printer_change` accepts any saved printer's name, not just the one the chat is about.
- In the prompt test runs, models called `printer_add` and `printer_identify` in change chats.

**What the published guidance says** (Anthropic and OpenAI docs; research cited in my notes):
- Eight tools is too few for the number itself to matter. Accuracy problems start around 20–50 tools.
- The known failure is tools offered where they don't belong, or that overlap. That's what we have.
- Enforce which actions are allowed in each state in code. Hiding a tool doesn't replace the app refusing it.
- OpenAI's API, which the app uses, can restrict which tools may be called (`allowed_tools`) while still sending the full list. The prompt cache and the guide's "same tools on every request" rule both stay intact.

**My recommendation:**
1. **Decide the allowed tools from the chat's state, not just its mode:**

   | Chat state | Allowed tools |
   |---|---|
   | Adding, nothing added yet | identify, add, full list, finish |
   | Adding, after a printer is added | also change, connect, check connection, printer settings, so "add then connect" still works |
   | Change or Connect | change, connect, check connection, printer settings, finish; no add, lookup or full list |

2. **Make the app refuse anything else,** in the class that manages the chat (`PrinterConversation`), with a clear error the model can recover from. That follows the repo's own rule that the layer owning a decision enforces it.
3. **Fill in the printer from the chat instead of asking the model for it,** so `printer_change` can only touch the printer the chat is about.
4. **Send the allowed set with each request** through `tool_choice.allowed_tools`, keeping the full tool list the same. The prompt test script would do the same for DeepSeek. I haven't confirmed that OpenRouter passes this setting through; if it doesn't, the app's refusal still covers it.
5. **Update the guide and `architecture.md`** to describe this.
6. **Test it:**
   - C++ unit tests that each state's allowed set is correct and that out-of-place calls are refused;
   - one prompt test where someone in a change chat asks to add a different printer;
   - rerun the whole suite, old against new.

This is a C++ change inside the JusPrin folder (no upstream Orca files), and no bigger than the prompt fix. Want me to go ahead with it?
